ξουθόπτερος.definition: with nimble wings, E.HF487, Fr.467.4, Lyr.Alex.Adesp.7.13

ξυήλη.definition: Dor. , whittle, curved knife used in shaping a javelin, X.Cyr.6.2.32; as a weapon, Id.An.4.7.16, cf. 4.8.25

ξυλαλόη.definition: = Aët.1.131; scanned ⏑–⏑– by Heraclit. Gramm. in An.Ox.3.277

ξυνήϊος.definition: Ep. and Ion. , common : neut. pl. common stock, Il.1.124, 23.809

ξύνημα.definition: javelin-throwing on horseback while on the wheel, Celtic word, Arr.Tact.42.4

ξυνήων.definition: as Adj., the salt on the common table, Alex.Aet.3.15

ξυνοδοτήρ.definition: bounteous giver, epith. of Apollo, AP9.525.15

ξυράφιον.definition: Dim. of Sch.Ar.Ach.849; surgical knife, Gal.14.786

ξυρόν.definition: razor, E.El.241, Ar.Ec.65, Th.219, Nic.Al.411, Plu.Art.29, etc.: prov., . . , death or life is balanced on a razor's edge, Il.10.173: freq. in later authors, to express a delicately balanced like lihood of failure or …

ξυρός.definition: = Archipp.45, Alciphr.3.66, v.l. in AP11.288 ; prov. of lucky meetings, Suid

ξυστιδωτός.definition: garment with ornament in strigil form , IG22.1514.11

ξυστίς.definition: robe of rich and soft material; = Epich.97, Diph.52. fabric, such as fustian, plush, velvet, etc. ; cf. IV, 3 : for the semantic relation between and , and cf. ONorse skrúd 'some kind of textile fabric', skrúd-kloedi …

ξῦστρον.definition: scythe fixed to chariots, D.S.17.53; = BSA27.228 : condemned by Thom.Mag.p.252 R

ξανθίζω.definition: make yellow or brown, by roasting or; intr., to be yellow, LXXLe.13.30; Alciphr.Fr.5.4

ξάνθιον.definition: a plant used for dyeing the hair yellow

ξάνθισμα.definition: that which is dyed yellow, dyed hair, E.Fr.322, cf. AP5.259

ξανθοδερκής.definition: with fiery eyes, of a dragon, B.8.12

ξανθόθριξ.definition: gen. yellow-haired, Sol.22 , Theoc.18.1; Aglaïas13; of a horse, chestnut, B.5.37

ξανθοκάρηνος.definition: with yellow head, of Dionysus, AP9.524.15

ξανθόχολος.definition: suffering from jaundice, Ruf.Fr.80, Aët.3.66, dub. in Sch.Il.1.197

ξανθόχροος.definition: with yellow skin, Mosch.2.84: heterocl. acc. Nonn.D.11.180

ξανθόχρως.definition: = foreg., brown, of fried fish, Nausicr.2.7

ξανθόω.definition: dye yellow, Ps.-Democr.Alch.p.52 B.:—Pass., become yellow, Dsc.1.68

ξάνιον.definition: card for combing wool, Poll.5.96, AB284; = Poll.6.90,10.101

ξάντρια.definition: fem. of = putatrix, Gloss.: name of a play by Aeschylus

ξεινοβάκχη.definition: mad for love of the stranger, of Medea, Lyc.175

ξεναγέτης.definition: one who takes charge of guests, the hospitable Delphians, Pi.N.7.43

ξεναγέω.definition: to be a leader of mercenaries; guide strangers, show them the sights, your work as a guide has been done excellently, Pl.Phdr.230c; one seeing the sights, ibid. ; Luc.DMort.18.1, cf. Cont.I : metaph., generally, guide…

ξεναγία.definition: office of command of a body of; = Ael.Tact.9.4, Arr.Tact.10.3

ξεναγός.definition: commander of mercenary; commander of a I.2, Ael.Tact.9.4, Arr.Tact.10.3

ξεναπάτης.definition: one who betrays his host, Ibyc.Oxy.1790i10, E.Med.1392; a treacherous breeze within a harbour, while another is blowing at sea, AB109

ξένη.definition: foreign woman, A.Ag.950, etc; foreign country, S.Ph.135; X.Lac.14.4; Phld.Rh.2.146S., cf. Plu.2.576c, etc

ξενηλασία.definition: at Sparta, expulsion of foreigners, X.Lac.14.4: mostly in pl., Th.1.144, 2.39, Pl.Prt.342c, Lg.950b, Arist.Pol.1272b17

ξενηλατέω.definition: banish foreigners, in Pass., Ar.Av.1013, Plb.9.29.4, D.S.40.3

ξενία.definition: friendly relation between two states, or between a person and a foreign state, Lat. hospitium facere cum aliquo, Hdt.1.27,3.39; Id.7.116; Id.1.69; Id.4.154; Isoc.4.43; because of their friendly relations, Th.8.6; Plu.…

ξενίζω.definition: Ion. and Ep. fut. later; surprise, astonish by some strange sight, Plb.3.114.4; of strange words, Hld.6.14; Gp.2.48.2; do violence to the ordinary use of language, Simp.in Cael.679.28:—Pass., to be astonished, S.Ichn.…

ξένιος.definition: Ion. (as always in Hdt., and; Att. , friendly gifts, given to the guest by his host, esp. meat and drink, Il.11.779, cf.18.387, Od.5.91, etc.; 9.229, cf. 19.185 ); . . as a friendly gift, A.Ag.1590; X.HG7.2.3, cf. PCa…

ξένισις.definition: entertainment of a guest or stranger, Th.6.46

ξενισμός.definition: = foreg., Pl.Ly.205c, Luc.Salt.45, etc; strangeness, novelty, Plb.15.17.1, D.S.3.33

ξενιτεία.definition: living abroad, LXXWi.18.3, Aristeas249; life of a mercenary in foreign service, Democr.246, PSI1.76.8

ξενιτεύω.definition: live abroad, Timae.139, Nic.Dam.1032 J; Med., to be a mercenary in foreign service, Isoc.5.122, Ep.2.19; Antiph.96

ξενοδαΐκτης.definition: Dor. one who murders guests or strangers, Pi.Parth.Fr.13.30; prob. cj. in E.HF391

ξενοδαίτης.definition: Dor. one that devours guests or strangers, of the Cyclops, Id.Cyc.658

ξενοδοκέω.definition: Ion. entertain guests or; testify, Pi.Fr.311:— Med., Hsch

ξενοδόκος.definition: Ion. and one who receives; witness, Simon.84.7, cf. Hsch.—The forms are condemned by Moer.p.271 P., Thom.Mag.p.251 R.; cf

ξενοδοχεῖον.definition: place for strangers to lodge in, inn, Jul.Ep.84a, Cod.Just.1.2.15.1, Just.Nov.120.1 Intr., PSI4.284.2, Suid., etc

ξενοδοχία.definition: entertainment of a stranger, X.Oec.9.10 , Thphr.Char.23.9

ξενοδώτης.definition: dub. sens., epith. of Dionysus, AP9.524.15

ξενοκαδής.definition: caring for strangers, Pi.Pae. Oxy.841 Fr.131

ξενοκλείδειον.definition: fund derived from Xenoclides, Inscr. Délos320 B78

ξενοκρατέομαι.definition: Pass., to be in the power of mercenary troops, Aen. Tact.12.4

ξενοκτονέω.definition: Ion. slay guests or strangers, Hdt.2.115, E.Hec.1247, D.S.4.18

ξενοκτονία.definition: murder of strangers, Id.1.88, D.H.1.41; murder of a guest, Plu.2.319d; of a host, Id.Dio54

ξενοκτόνος.definition: slaying guests or strangers, E.IT53, Aeschin.3.224; Scymn.669, cf. Plu.Mar.8

ξενολογέω.definition: enlist foreign troops, esp. mercenaries; metaph., raise a contribution of pity, D.S.34/5.2.39

ξενολογία.definition: recruitment of mercenaries, Arist.Oec.1353b11, Plb.15.25.16, D.S.18.61

ξενολόγιον.definition: army of mercenaries, Plb.29.23.6, 31.17.1, SIG581.40 , OGI437.67, 71

ξενολόγος.definition: enlisting mercenaries, Plb.1.32.1,5.63.9, D.S.14.62, Plu.Dio23; title of a comedy by Menander

ξενομανέω.definition: have a rage for foreign fashions, Plu.2.527f

ξενοπαθέω.definition: have a strange feeling, Plu.Phil.12; Id.2.607e; ib.601c, cf. Sor.1.81

ξενοπολίτης.definition: pertaining to an alien, Id.in Rh.3.670 W

ξενοπρεπής.definition: strange, out of the way, Hp Fract.1, D.H.Dem.34, Aret.SD2.13 . Adv. Steph.in Hp.2.288 D

ξενοπρόσωπος.definition: only in Adv. with reference to a person other than oneself, Sch.Aristid.p.430 D

ξενόστασις.definition: lodging for guests or strangers, S.OC90; Id.Fr.274

ξενοτροφέω.definition: maintain mercenary troops, Th.7.48, Isoc.8.46, Aen. Tact.13.1, D.11.18, LXX2 Ma.10.14, Plu.2.214d; D.S.1.67:—Pass., Aen. Tact.13.4

ξενοτροφία.definition: maintenance of mercenaries, Hyp.Fr.256, Aen. Tact.13:1 tit

ξενοφόνος.definition: poet. murdering strangers; honour paid to murderers of strangers, E.IT776

ξενοφυής.definition: strange of shape or nature, Tz.H.8.579, 636

ξενοφύλαξ.definition: in pl., magistrates charged with the protection of foreigners, Rev.Et. Gr.42.35

ξενοφωνέω.definition: speak or sound strangely, use out-of-the- way words, Dexipp.in Cat.6.17, Sophon.in de An.47.12:—Pass., to be disconcerted by strange expressions, Olymp.Alch.p.86 B.; so intr. in Act., Sch.Il.23.403

ξενόφωνος.definition: speaking or sounding strange, rejected by Poll.2.113

ξενόω.definition: Ion. make one's friend and; mostly in Pass., with fut. Med. S.Ph.303: pf. aor

ξενών.definition: guest-chamber, in pl., E.Alc.543, 547; Com.Adesp.1211, cf. D.S.13.83, J.BJ5.4.4: sg., Pl.Ti.20c; = OGI609.21 , Just.Nov.59.3; cf

ξέσμα.definition: that which is smoothed or; abrasion, in pl., Jul.Caes.309c

ξέστης.definition: formed from Lat. sextarius, a Roman; pitcher, cup, Ev.Marc.7.4, POxy.921.23 , Harp.Astr.inCat.Cod.Astr.8.139

ξεστιαῖος.definition: of a Gal.13.435, cf. Phlp.in Mete.24.24

ξέω.definition: impf. Od.23.199: fut. Paul.Aeg.3.22.12; carve wood, shape by carving, Od.23.199; Simon.l.c.:—Pass., Hld.l.c

ξηραίνω.definition: drain dry, Th.1.109; metaph., Telesp.34 H

ξηραλοιφέω.definition: rub dry with oil, of wrestlers, Lex Solonis ap. Plu.Sol.1 , S.Fr.494, Plu.2.152d, Philostr.Gym.58, D.C.77.11; opp. Gal.11.532

ξηραλοιφία.definition: rubbing dry with oil, Eust.764.13, Suid

ξηραμπέλινος.definition: of the colour of withered vine- leaves, bright red, scarlet, [vestes] xerampelinae Juv.6.519; Lyd.Mag.1.17; Suid. s.v

ξηρασία.definition: Ion. desiccation; dryness, Str.2.3.7; Dsc.2.142, cf. LXXJd.6.37; become dry, Agatharch.34

ξηρίον.definition: desiccative powder for putting on wounds, POxy.1142.7 , Aët.6.65,al., Alex.Trall.1.15; Alex.Aphr.Pr.1.150

ξηροκολλούριον.definition: dry, i.e. thick, eye-salve, Gal.12.725, Alex.Trall.2

ξηρολουσία.definition: taking a dry bath, i.e. in hot sand, Cass.Fel.76

ξηρολουτρέω.definition: take a dry bath, i.e. roll in hot sand, Hsch

ξηρόμυρον.definition: dry perfume, i.e. in cake or powder; = rosmarinum, Gloss

ξηροποιέω.definition: make dry, dry up, v.l. in Dsc.5.103

ξηροπυρία.definition: Medic., application of dry heat, Aët.16.29, Sch.Nic.Al.586, Gloss

ξηροφαγέω.definition: eat dry food, AP11.205 , Dsc.Eup.2.65, Sor.1.49

ξηροφαγία.definition: eating of dry food, Chrysipp.Tyan. ap. Ath.3.113b, Gal.14.751; herbs ealen raw, Gloss

ξηρόφορτον.definition: weight of a cargo of fruit after drying, OGI629.164

ξηρόφωνος.definition: with a husky voice, Sch.D ll.13.41; of the twang of a bowstring, Eust.1914.42

ξιφηφόρος.definition: bearing a sword, sword in hand; = II, Sch.Arat.1091

ξιφίας.definition: sword fish, Arist.HA505a18; a kind of comet , Plin.HN 2.89

ξίφιον.definition: or corn-flag, Gladiolus segetum, Thphr.HP6.8.1, Dsc.4.20

ξίφισμα.definition: = sq., Choerob. in An.Ox.2.242, cf. Hsch

ξιφοδήλητος.definition: slain by the sword, death by the sword, A.Ag.1528, Ch.729

ξιφοδρέπανον.definition: sickle-shaped sword, scimitar, Ph.Bel.99.51, POxy.1241 vi 22; = Hsch

ξιφοειδής.definition: sword-shaped, Thphr.HP7.13.1, Str.3.5.10; Gal.2.496; the ensiform cartilage, Id.UP6.3, al

ξιφοκτόνος.definition: slaying with the sword, S.Aj.10; E.Hel.354

ξιφουλκία.definition: drawing of a sword, Plu.Arist.18 , Pomp.69

ξοανηφόρος.definition: image-bearer: title of a play by Sophocles

ξόανον.definition: image carved of wood, E.Ion1403; musical instrument, S.Fr.238

ξοΐς.definition: chisel, IG22.463.40, 11.199A87 , Supp.Epigr.4.447.40 , etc. ; toothed chisel, IG7.3073.104 ; , ib.148; Inscr.Délos507; APl.4.86

ξυλαμάω.definition: plant or sow, usu. of green crops or fodder , mostly c. dat., POxy.499.15 , PSI4.315.10 ; POxy.1629.10 ; but also PFlor.85.21

ξυλάριον.definition: Dim. of small piece of wood, twig, LXX3 Ki.17.12, Dsc.1.70, Gal.12.422; log, BGU824.12 , cf. POxy.1292.12 , etc

ξυλεία.definition: felling and carrying of wood; timber, Plb.3.42.3

ξυλεύς.definition: woodcutter, of a sacrificial attendant, SIG1021.31 , Paus.5.13.2,5.15.10, Hsch

ξυλεύω.definition: cut wood, SIG685.82 , IPE12.403 B :—Med., Men.Mon.123, cf. Hsch.; cf

ξυλήφιον.definition: Dim. of piece of wood, stick, Hp.Steril.230, Alex.98.24, Plb.6.34.9, D.S.4.76:—misspelt D.S.l.c. , Thom.Mag.p.253 R. ; v.l. in Suid. s.vv. EM611.23

ξυλίζομαι.definition: Med., gather wood, X.An.2.4.11; Plu.Art.25; Alciphr.1.1

ξύλινος.definition: of wood, wooden, Pi.P.3.38; metaph., wooden, AP11.275 , cf. 255

ξυλίτης.definition: like wood: name of a fish, Hsch; timber-bearing land, PPetr.3p.223 , PCair.Zen.387.9 , PLille 5.20 ; later opp. PLond.2.267.99 , BGU703.5

ξυλοβάλσαμον.definition: balsam-wood, Str.16.2.41, Dsc.1.19, Plin.HN 12.118, Gal.10.466, Gp.7.13.4

ξυλογραφέομαι.definition: Pass., to be written upon wood, Test. Epict.8.24,30

ξυλοειδής.definition: like wood, Clytus I; wooden, PSI5.547.15, al

ξυλοκασία.definition: an inferior kind of cassia, Gal.19.738, Edict.Diocl. 32.53, Aët.16.130

ξυλοκέρατον.definition: Ceratonia Siliqua, Alex.Trall.9.3, Steph.in Hp.1.211 D., cf. Gloss

ξυλόκερκος.definition: a gate at Constantinople, AP9.690 tit

ξυλοκιννάμωμον.definition: wood of cinnamon, Dsc.1.14, Plin.HN12.91, Gal.13.185, Gp.8.22.2

ξυλοκοπέω.definition: cut wood, make a clearance, PLille 5.24; beat with a stick, cudgel, of the Roman fustuarium, Plb.6.37.1 , 6.38.1: generally, Arr.Epict.3.7.33:—Pass., ib.4.4.37, POxy.706.13

ξυλοκόπος.definition: hewing, felling wood; Subst. wood-feller, LXXJo.9.27, Str.16.4.11

ξυλοκύμβη.definition: nickname of an ill-favoured woman, Com.Adesp.1091

ξυλομετρέω.definition: measure by , i. e. measure the amount of earth excavated, Wilcken Chr.389.27

ξυλομέτρης.definition: official charged with the measuring of earth excavated, PLond.5.1648.8, 13

ξυλοπέδη.definition: log of wood tied to the feet, Aq.Jb.13.27,33.11

ξυλοπυρία.definition: perh. sharpening to a point with fire, Anon.in Rh.236.8

ξυλοστεγής.definition: covered with wood, prob. in POxy.2146.13

ξυλόστομος.definition: wooden mouthed, of horses, prob. cj. in Hippiatr.115

ξυλοτόμος.definition: woodcutter, Sammelb.4874: as Adj., v.l. in X.Cyr.6.2.36

ξυλουργία.definition: working of wood, carpentry, A.Pr.451, IG12.347.35

ξυλοφάγος.definition: eating wood, Str.12.7.3; cj. for Ant.Lib.22.5

ξυλοφθόρον.definition: an insect that destroys wood, Arist.HA557b13 codd

ξυλοφορέω.definition: carry wood, of a slave or mule; carry a stick, as the Cynics did, Luc.Pisc.24

ξυλοφόριος.definition: belonging to a wood-offering, the Jewish feast of Tabernacles, J.BJ2.17.6

ξυλόφρακτος.definition: fenced with wood, = pons sublicius, D.H.3.55,5.24, 9.68

ξύλοχος.definition: thicket, copse, Il.5.162; 11.415, 21.573; . . in his lair, Od.4.335, cf. 19.445; AP7.445 : also in late Prose, Palaeph.14: pl., Stud.Pont.3.16 , Coluth.42, Anacreont.29.5

ξυλόω.definition: turn into wood :—Pass., become wood; make of wood, IG11.203 A53 , cf. 12.1270.15 , LXX2 Ch.3.5:—Pass., ib.Ez.41.16; SIG996.18

ξυλών.definition: place for wood, wood-house, ib.159 A 56, al. , Inscr.Délos399 A85 , Gloss

ξύλωσις.definition: wood-work of a building, Th.2.14; Milet.3.32 , J.AJ3.6.5

ξυνοχαρής.definition: rejoicing with all alike, of Apollo, ibid

ξυνόω.definition: cause to participate, Nonn.D.17.220:—Med., = Nearch. ap. Arr.Ind.20.4, Man.2.493

ξυρέω.definition: Trag. and Att. ; Plu.2.180b, Artem.1.22 ; both forms in codd. of Hdt.; cf. fut. LXXDe.21.12: aor. Hp.Aff.4, Hdt.5.35, etc. :—Med., fut. LXXEz.44.20, J.BJ2.15.1, Hsch. s.v. aor. LXXNu.6.19, al., Luc.DMeretr.12.5:—Pass.…

ξύρησις.definition: shaving, Asclep. ap. Gal.12.413, Plu.2.352c, Archig. ap. Aët.6.28, Alex.Aphr.Pr.2.36; baldness, LXXIs.22.12

ξυρίζω.definition: = Sch.Nic.Al.410:—Med., fut. inf. f.l. for Alciphr.3.66

ξύρω.definition: collat. form for impf. Luc.Pseudol.27: aor. part. Hp.Morb.3.1, Tz.H.9.231:—Med., have oneself shaved, Chrysipp.Stoic.3.198; Plu.2.352c : aor. I, ib.336e, cf. Luc.Syr.D.53,55, Alciphr.3.43

ξύσμα.definition: filings, shavings, Hp.Aph.7.68; lint, Erot. s.v

ξυσμάτιον.definition: Dim. of I.1c, Hp.Epid.7.84; strip of linen, Aët.8.27

ξυσμή.definition: in pl., scratchings, i.e. critical marks in; scab, as a term of abuse, Sophr.53

ξυσταρχέω.definition: hold the office of Rev.Arch.1916.338 , PLond.3.1178.58

ξυστάρχης.definition: president of an athletic association, . . IG 3.1171, cf. POxy.1050.7 , Sammelb.5725, etc. ; IGRom.4.1215 , IG14.1102, al

ξυσταρχία.definition: office of SIG1073.9 : in pl., IGRom.4.1419b1, Delph.3.466.6

ξυστήρ.definition: scraper, rasp, file, Hp.VC14; part of the external ear, Gal.14.701

ξυστήριος.definition: of or for scraping: dentist's instrument for scaling teeth, Paul.Aeg.6.28

ξυστόν.definition: spear, E.Hec.920 ; a horseman's lance, X.Cyr.4.5.58, cf. 7.1.33, Plu.Aem.16: pl. Jul.Or.2.60a codd

ξυστοφορέω.definition: carry a lance, in Pass. , Alc.Oxy.1789 Fr.1i8

ξυστοφόρος.definition: lance-bearing, of horsemen, X.Cyr.7.5.41, 8.3.16, Plb.5.53.2, D.S.19.27, Ascl.Tact.2.12, Arr.Tact.4.4, Plu.Flam.17

ξύστρα.definition: scraper used after bathing, Hp.Nat.Mul.42; = Archig. ap. Gal.12.620

ξυστρίον.definition: Dim. of PLond.2.191.8 (ii A; small raspatory at the end of a forceps, Paul.Aeg.6.25

ξυστροειδής.definition: shaped like a Erot.s.v. Procl.in Euc.pp.127,238 F

ξυστρολήκυθος.definition: slave who carried his master's and to and from the bath, Hsch

ξυστροφύλαξ.definition: place or box for keeping in, Artem.1.64

ξύω.definition: shred, prob. in Hp.Int.37; Thphr.HP9.11.2; shape by whittling, shaving, or planing, ib.5.1.7:—Med., whittle oneself a javelin, X.l.c
